Whittaker coefficients in quantum geometric Langlands program

Abstract

We study Whittaker coefficients in the context of quantum geometric Langlands program.

In the first part of this work, we prove that for any semisimple group G cuspidal automor-

phic twisted D-modules have non-vanishing quantum Whittaker coefficients. The argument

provides a microlocal interpretation of the Whittaker coefficients functor for any ˇΛ+-valued

divisor under some hypothesis on singular support.

In the second part, we use quantum Whittaker coefficients functor to construct the quan-

tum geometric Langlands functor in the Betti setting. We show that the functor is compat-

ible with the 2-Fourier-Mukai equivalence between sheaves of categories over 2-stacks GeZG

and Geπ1( ˇG), which classify gerbes on X with respect to the center ZG of G and algebraic

fundamental group π1( ˇG) of the Langlands dual group ˇG.

### 1.1.1 Metaplectic groups.

The metaplectic group Mp2n(R) is the double cover of the symplectic group Sp2n(R). It was

defined in parallel to the Spin(n) group, which is the double cover of the special orthogonal

group SO(n, R), and is an important tool in quantum mechanics.

Although there is a topological characterization of Mp2n(R), this group is not R-points

of a linear algebraic group [Wei23, Theorem 2.1]. Therefore, it is a priori unclear how to

generalize the notion beyond R. In [Wei64], Weil constructed Mp2n(R) as a group of unitary

operators on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space L2(Rn).

A prominent feature of his construction is that it works with R replaced by any local

field. Moreover, it extends to the adelic setting: for a global field F Weil defined the double

cover f Sp2n(AF) of Sp2n(AF), which splits over Sp2n(F). This suggests a generalization of the

theory of automorphic functions for Sp2n.

### 1.1.2 Works of Brylinski and Deligne.

Brylinski and Deligne ([BD01]), motivated by the result of Matsumoto, studied classification

of extensions of a reductive group G over k by K2 viewed as sheaves of groups on the

big Zariski site of k. They have described the groupoid of such extensions in combinatorial

terms. For instance, for a split semi-simple simply-connected group G the category of central

extentions of G by K2 is equivalent to the category whose objects are W-invariant Z-valued

bilinear forms on the cocharacter lattice of the torus T ⊂G, and whose only morphisms are

identity on each object.

We emphasize that given such an extension eG, one is automatically in position to extend

the theory of automorphic forms on G(AF) to eG(AF). However, the heart of the study of

automorphic form is the Langlands correspondence, i.e. the connection to the representa-

tions of the Galois group Gal( ¯F/F) valued in the L-group LG, constructed via root data of

G. In [Wei18], Weissman defined a version of the L-group for Brylinki–Deligne extensions,

thereby generalizing Langlands conjecture to the setting of eG, which we will call arithmetic

metaplectic Langlands correspondence.

### 1.1.3 Geometric picture.

Recall that unramified automorphic forms are functions on the double coset

G(F)\G(AF)/G(OF). An element of G(AF)/G(OF) can be interpreted as a pair (E, βη),

where E is a G-bundle on X and βη is a section of E over a generic point η of X. A geomet-

ric gadget that encodes this data is the Beilinson–Drinfeld affine Grassmannian GrG,Ran, an

object of algebraic geometry, whose k-points are (E, β) and a specified collection of points of

X where β might not exist. By definition, GrG,Ran lives over moduli space Ran of collections

of points of X. Beilinson and Drinfeld observed that GrG,Ran carries a natural factorization

structure, meaning that

GrG,Ran ×Ran(x1, x2) =: GrG,(x1,x2) ∼= GrG,x1 × GrG,x2

The analogy between G(AF)/G(OF) and GrG,Ran, and classification of line bundles on

Theorem 1.1.4 ([TZ21]). The groupoid of central extensions of G by K2 is canonically

### 1.2.5 Topological factorization homology.

The theory of factorization homology derives from the factorization algebras of Beilinson

and Drinfeld ([BD04]), and is a topological version of their theory. Factorization homology

with coefficients in n-disk algebras are homology theories for topological manifolds satisfying

a generalization of the Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms for ordinary homology; as such, it gener-

alizes ordinary homology in a way that is only defined on n-manifolds and not necessarily

tum field theories ([CG17]). An important special case is that of associative algebras where

factorization homology over the circle recovers Hochschild homology.

### 1.3 Whittaker coefficients.

### 1.3.1 Hecke action.

One important property required of the arithmetic Langlands correpondence is that certain

natural invariants attached to the Galois representations and to the automorphic represen-

tations be matched. These invariants are the Frobenius conjugacy classes on the Galois

side and the Hecke eigenvalues on the automorphic side, which are identified via Satake iso-

morphism. In the geometric terms, this translates as follows. The category of automoprhic

sheaves carries a family of commuting Hecke operations given by elements V ∈Rep( ˇG) (resp.

V ∈Rep(H) in the metaplectic situation) for every point x ∈X. Then we have:

Theorem 1.3.2. For every irreducible ˇG-local system σ there exists a unique Hecke eigen-

sheaf with eigenvalue σ.
